_meta.description: CDM methodologies relevant to waste-to-energy and related project types
_meta.refresh_process: Download current methodology list from UNFCCC CDM registry; update IDs, versions, and applicability conditions

methodologies.name: Alternative Waste Treatment Processes
applicability_conditions: The project treats waste that would have been disposed at a SWDS
Uses composting, anaerobic digestion, gasification, RDF, or other alternative treatment
Not exclusively biomass residues from agricultural activities
No methane recovery in baseline scenario
Fossil fuel co-firing does not exceed 50% of total energy input

methodologies.name: Emissions Reduction Through Partial Substitution of Fossil Fuels with Alternative Fuels in Cement or Quicklite Manufacture
applicability_conditions: Partial substitution of fossil fuels in cement/quicklite manufacturing
Alternative fuel is biomass residue, RDF, or waste-derived fuel
Alternative fuel not used in baseline at the project facility
No new cement manufacturing capacity

methodologies.name: Electricity and Heat Generation from Biomass
applicability_conditions: Generates electricity and/or heat using biomass as fuel
Biomass from renewable sources
Displaces fossil fuel-based generation
Not fuel switching between fossil fuels

methodologies.name: Avoided Emissions from Organic Waste Through Alternative Waste Treatment Processes
applicability_conditions: Avoids methane from disposal of organic waste at SWDS
Waste would have been disposed in SWDS in baseline
Uses composting, anaerobic digestion, or biological treatment
Does not involve combustion or thermal treatment

methodologies.name: Flaring or Use of Landfill Gas
applicability_conditions: Captures and combusts or uses landfill gas from existing SWDS
No LFG capture in baseline
Not required by regulation to capture LFG
Captured gas combusted in flare, engine, turbine, or boiler

methodologies.name: Methane Emissions Reduction from Organic Waste Water and Bioorganic Waste
applicability_conditions: Reduces methane from organic wastewater or bioorganic waste treatment
Methane would have been released to atmosphere in baseline
Project introduces controlled anaerobic treatment with methane capture
Captured methane is flared or used for energy generation

methodologies.name: Avoidance of Methane Production from Decay of Biomass Through Controlled Combustion, Gasification or Mechanical/Thermal Treatment
applicability_conditions: Avoids methane from biomass decay through controlled treatment
Small-scale (<=60,000 tCO2e/year)
Waste would have decayed uncontrolled in baseline
No fossil fuel co-firing above 50%
